parsed_response.reasoning: The diff shows BaseCalendarService.createEvent was updated to use `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and still filters calendars via `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId`, with no use of the newly added `credentialId` parameter (the Calendar interface now requires `createEvent(event, credentialId)`). Meanwhile EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now iterates every destination in `event.destinationCalendar` and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` per host, so for CalDav/Apple providers every per-host call is filtered against only the first host's externalId — non-primary hosts' destination calendars are dropped, the exact multi-host case the PR enables for Google. The mechanism is grounded in visible diff lines; whether the surrounding CalDav implementation mitigates it is unverifiable, but the described defect follows directly from the shown code.

judged_text: BaseCalendarService.createEvent (parent of the CalDav/Apple services) still filters calendars against destinationCalendar[0] and ignores the new credentialId argument, so the credential-aware target selection introduced for Google is absent for every provider built on this base class. Collective bookings with multiple CalDav/Apple destination calendars create every per-host event in the first host's calendar (or fail per credential), so non-primary hosts' calendars never receive the event — the exact multi-host scenario this PR claims to fix silently does not work outside Google.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Calendar interface to `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)` and CalendarManager now calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` for all providers. However, `BaseCalendarService` (used by CalDav/Apple-derived services) still selects the target calendar solely by destructuring the first element of `event.destinationCalendar` (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`) and filtering calendars by that single `externalId`. There is no credentialId-based selection analogous to the new Google logic (`find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`). With `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now passing an event whose `destinationCalendar` may contain multiple hosts' destinations, this base implementation will either (a) always target the first host's calendar, or (b) filter out all calendars for other credentials (if their calendar list doesn't contain the first host's externalId), causing missing events for non-primary hosts. This directly matches the finding and is a correctness defect exposed by the refactor.
